name: Bright violet
lede: Bright violet is a descriptive name for a vivid purple, and the best history the books offer is a very old theory of how violet is made.

sections.title: Bright plus violet
sections.body: The name joins bright to [[violet]]. Our sources list it in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system and in the 2010 xkcd survey [1]. The nearest ISCC-NBS name is "brilliant violet" at a distance of 11.9, and the xkcd list gives a different, more saturated purple, #AD0AFD, under the same words [1]. Compare [[vivid-violet]], [[royal-purple]] and [[purple]].

sections.title: Ancient theories and a logwood lake
sections.body:
Birren quotes Aristotle, who explained a vivid bright violet as weak sunlight mixed with a thin, dusky white [2]. That is an old theory of color, not modern evidence, and Birren's own history of such claims is treated as contested [2].

In the pigment books, Vegetable violet was a bright violet lake based on logwood, according to Mayer [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [4].
